brief: September payrolls missed DB's forecast: headline +29k vs. +133k expected and private +46k vs. +127k, plus 60k of downward revisions to the prior two months. Average hourly earnings grew only +0.1% vs. +0.3% expected, which DB attributes partly to a still-elevated 34.4-hour workweek; its own payroll-proxy measure of labor income growth slipped only a tenth to 4.2%, still supportive of consumer spending. The household survey was more mixed: unemployment edged up to 4.175% from 4.141%, but U-6 fell to 7.6%, and a 78k rise in household unemployment alongside a 406k employment gain lifted participation to 61.8%, its highest since last May, with prime-age participation and employment ratios continuing to recover. DB reads the report as consistent with a still-stable labor market and keeps its baseline of two more 25bp Fed hikes over the next couple of quarters; Wednesday's FOMC minutes may clarify how far officials think the neutral rate has risen. DB's Q3 GDP forecast stands at 3.3% annualized. September's bond selloff (2yr +40bps, 10yr +50bps) reflected real-yield repricing of both Fed policy and longer-term growth expectations, which DB says helps explain resilient risk assets even as financial conditions, per its FCI-G tracker, remain a tailwind to growth.
